difference.candidate_requirement: A report outbound admission must fail closed when the sender Sent Maildir path is not a real directory. Return HTTP 200 with the exact per-delivery error=outbound queue unavailable, consume only bounded task-ID allocators, leave PostgreSQL, Redis projections, email indexes, Maildir files, and temporary files unchanged, and allow one explicit retry after the path is restored.
difference.oracle_behavior: Frozen Java allocates a Redis task ID and then swallows the Maildir exception in the outbound service. It still initializes the domain hash, writes task metadata with sentFileName and sentSubdirectory absent, and appends the task ID to pending; the report route returns success even though no Sent file exists.
difference.candidate_behavior: Rust returns the bounded failed DMARC delivery result, advances only the Redis sequence and PostgreSQL identity allocator, publishes no Redis task/domain/pending state, creates no outbound or email-index row, leaves no spool or temporary file, and succeeds once after the Sent directory is restored.
difference.reason: Publishing a queue task without a durable Sent message makes later delivery and recovery unsafe and can lose or duplicate reports. The replacement must preserve atomic Maildir publication and fail closed rather than reproduce the Java partial-publication defect.
difference.scope: Only a deterministic regular-file replacement of the empty qa@example.test/sent directory during report email admission. Healthy Maildir publication, exact report MIME and gzip bytes, Redis keys and TTLs, PostgreSQL transaction semantics, source rows, DNS order, response status/content type, application continuity, recovery retry, and all non-faulted report behavior remain strict.

evidence.fault: Before the request, replace the absent or empty sender Sent directory with a regular marker file; restore the exact directory before the explicit retry.
